served: time of day / relation to sleep

results: 1. duration of the events: about 15 seconds
2. time of day / relation to sleep: predominantly out of sleep at night
3. head injury history: mild repetitive non-penetrating traumatic brain injury, none requiring hospitalisation
4. advanced diffusion imaging / tractography: multishell diffusion MRI showed disrupted white matter tracts
5. video-EEG monitoring of a typical event: the diagnosis was made on SEMIOLOGY from clinically documented video-EEG; there was NO interpretable ictal EEG correlate because of movement artefact
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Nocturnal frontal lobe epilepsy, secondary to repetitive traumatic brain injury.
Alternatives:
1. REM sleep behaviour disorder
2. Non-REM parasomnia (disorder of arousal)
3. Psychogenic non-epileptic seizures
dx: Nocturnal frontal lobe epilepsy, secondary to repetitive traumatic brain injury.
